text: Download for Mac or brew install --cask zigaowang/tap/zigzag Free and open source. macOS 15.4 or later. Your tabs in a sidebar, grouped into spaces. A native Mac app in Swift on WebKit, about 35 MB installed, with no account and no telemetry. Hi, I'm Zigao, a high school student in Shanghai. I used Arc every day. When The Browser Company said it's shutting Arc down on December 22, I really didn't want to go back to tabs along the top, and the alternatives I tried were either Chromium forks or browsers built around AI. So I made my own, and I've used it as my main browser ever since. Why WebKit and not Chromium? I actually started by forking Helium. The source was about 100 GB and every build took 3 to 4 hours on my Mac, which isn't something I can keep up by myself. WebKit already comes with macOS, it's lighter on battery and memory, and Apple ships its security fixes with macOS updates. You still get Chrome extensions, installed straight from the Chrome Web Store. Why not Zen or Orion? I tried both before starting this, and they're good. Zen runs on Firefox, so it uses Firefox extensions and doesn't feel like a Mac app to me. Orion is closer, but it isn't open source. I wanted something that works like Arc, feels native, is open source, and runs my Chrome extensions. Your Arc comes with you. File › Import from Another Browser…, pick Arc, and your spaces, pinned tabs, pinned folders, Favorites, history, passwords, sign-ins and extensions come over. Your open tabs can come too, split views and all, and wait to load until you click them; leave Open Tabs unchecked to start clean. If your spaces are on more than one Arc profile, each Arc profile comes over as a Zigzag profile of its own. 1Password works. Install it from the Chrome Web Store inside Zigzag, like you would in Arc. It talks to the 1Password app. The first time, add Zigzag in 1Password › Settings › Browser. Bitwarden works too. It can't be switched off. There's no account, and Zigzag doesn't depend on a server of mine. The only things I host are the update feed and a short list of ad blocking fixes, and if they went away, Zigzag would keep working. Privacy lists everything Zigzag connects to on its own. More, in motion, at zigzagbrowser.com . It's my everyday browser, but Zigzag is young and you'll find bugs. Things Arc users will notice: Zigzag is about 120,000 lines of Swift 6 and AppKit around WKWebView . There's no Chromium and no Electron: the engine is the WebKit that ships with macOS, which is why the app is small and why engine security fixes arrive with macOS updates rather than from me. The source is organized by feature: Sidebar , Tabs , Web , Extensions , Passwords , Import , Profiles , CommandBar , Desk (every tab at once), Peek , WebApps , Developer , MCP (AI apps), Settings , Window and Design (Zigzag's own drawn controls and design tokens). Over 2,000 tests cover importing, passwords, extensions, address handling, history, AI apps and the security fixes. No account, no analytics, no telemetry. Nothing about how you browse is sent to me. These are the only connections Zigzag makes on its own, apart from the pages you open: Translation runs on your Mac, with Apple's on-device Translation. Fraudulent website warnings are WebKit's own, the same as Safari's. Passwords stay in your Mac's Keychain and sync only through your own iCloud Keychain. Help › Report a Problem writes a report you can read first, and nothing is sent unless you send it. Download the DMG from zigzagbrowser.com , open it, and drag Zigzag to Applications. Or, with Homebrew: brew install --cask zigaowang/tap/zigzag Updates install by themselves. What changed in each version is in the release notes and CHANGELOG.md . Requirements: macOS 15.4 or later, Xcode 26 or later, and XcodeGen . brew install xcodegen git clone https://github.com/ZigaoWang/zigzag.git cd zigzag xcodegen generate open Zigzag.xcodeproj Run the Zigzag scheme. Debug builds run as a separate app, "Zigzag Dev", with their own data, so they never touch your everyday Zigzag. Signing is set up for my team. To build on your Mac, change two things in project.yml and run xcodegen generate again: Run the tests: xcodebuild test -project Zigzag.xcodeproj -scheme Zigzag Contributing Contributions are welcome.
